experience.description: Founder at Indē Wild

Post for Change is a unique not-for-profit organization that brings together the immense reach of social media influencers, their online platforms, the online generation, and the power of social media to achieve social change. We believe we are a unique NGO with the ability to reach, activate, and propel the online generation through the power of social media for social change in a way that has never been done before. We create a bridge between the power of social media influencers to non-governmental organizations with a focus to reduce the vast ocean of problems existing in the areas of equality for women, sexual rights, and mental health.

This NGO is the brainchild of leading Indian global influencer Diipa Bülller-Khosla and her husband, Oleg Büller-Khosla. We have conducted many campaigns in the last 2 years. Most recently, in partnership with UNICEF, Post for Change launched the second annual #RedDotChallenge in honor of Menstrual Hygiene Day 2020. Prominent figures including Dia Mirza & Aditi Rao Hydari took part in the challenge, sharing their own personal experiences. We achieved a reach of 201.5 million

Our 3 main goals for 2021 are:
1) EQUALITY FOR WOMEN: Economic independence and professional empowerment is an essential part of the UN’s Sustainable Development Goal for Gender Equality. PFC carries out campaigns that advance women’s professional and educational prospects.
2) SEXUAL RIGHTS: Our goal is to help destigmatize negative notions around periods, sex and sexual violence by working with organizations and influencers who want to use their voices to uplift female voices and the sexual, reproductive, and health rights for women globally.
3) MENTAL HEALTH: In a time where social media can warp peoples' sense of self, we're here to use social media as a powerful tool to do the opposite.  PFC aims to address issues that affect women's mental health and social acceptance. We believe in the power of social media to promote self-love and self-appreciation.

headline: I talk about Marketing, Branding, GTM Strategy, and Leadership | Documenting little parts of building a business, follow me to find new perspectives! 💜
about:
Hi! 
I work with SaaS, Fintech, D2C, and E-commerce brands across global markets—from the US and UK to Dubai, Kuwait, Qatar, Singapore, Japan, and India.

Founders usually reach out when something feels off.

→ Growth has slowed.
→ Conversions aren’t matching traffic.
→ The brand doesn’t reflect the product anymore.
→ Or they’re preparing for launch and don’t want to get it wrong.

I’ve spent the last 8+ years working closely with businesses at every stage—pre-launch strategy, post-launch pivots, scaling phases, messy funnels, evolving GTM strategies. And what I’ve learned is this:

The problem is rarely “do more marketing.”

It’s usually about alignment—between product, positioning, audience psychology, and execution.

Sometimes the positioning sounds impressive, but it doesn’t land.
Sometimes the funnel is leaking quietly while everyone blames ads.
Sometimes the product is solid,d but the narrative undersells it.
Sometimes the GTM looks great on a Notion board—and nowhere else.

That’s where I step in.

I go deeper than tactics. I look at the full picture—how the brand is perceived, how buyers are behaving, where friction is happening, and what actually needs to change to unlock the next stage of growth.

SaaS earns trust differently.
D2C builds desire differently.
E-commerce scales differently.

Treating them the same might be efficient. It’s rarely effective.

I’m deeply invested in understanding how people make decisions—and I actively integrate AI where it creates real leverage, not noise. Tools evolve. Buyer psychology evolves. Markets evolve. The thinking also has to evolve with it.

I work best with founders who are ambitious, open to being challenged, and serious about building something long-term while learning during the journey.

If that sounds like you, we should definitely connect and talk about your brand/idea.

publications.title: Raj Shamani: The ‘Useless Kid’ Influencing The World One Person At A Time
publications.description:
Raj Shamani: The ‘Useless Kid’ Influencing The World One Person At A Time

For someone who was frequently described as ‘lazy’ and ‘useless’ during his developmental stage as a young boy back in India, Raj Shamani has been able to overcome an unfavourable beginning and become a ray of hope to others facing the same challenges. 
Raj’s story is one of determination borne out of initial discouragement and negative perception especially from older folks; something many kids and young people today can relate with. Read on to find out more about this remarkable young man.

publications.title: Meet Raj Shamani: That Useless Kid’ That’s On A Mission To Make People Useful
publications.description:
Growing up as a young boy back in India, Raj Shamani would likely not have won any awards for ‘Most Promising Future’ amongst his peers. Frequently described with derogatory terms like ‘lazy’ and ‘useless,’ he stumbled through early school and life discouraged and disheartened. As expected, this kind of negative environment affected and impaired his self-esteem leading to poor performance in school and life.

This is the typical story of many youths that grow up to become a problem in the society, and it’s a direct result of the damaging words older people speak to them.

But not Raj. Raj decided to fight back at the downward direction his life was heading and to believe in himself. By taking that bold step and learning from great people around him, that young, obscure boy turned the tide to become a force to be reckoned with today.

publications.title: Top 5 young influencers of India
publications.description:
ndia is a highly populated country with many hidden talents which may or may not get the opportunity to grow. In these hard and difficult circumstances, there are many who are willing to take the extra effort to provide a better image of India around the globe. Visionaries, fashionistas, poets, influential speakers and more who are gaining a lot of exposure because of various global events and summits.

Today, we will talk about 5 such achievers who literally had nothing. They created and built themselves to achieve success. Have you ever had a wakeup call? I’m not talking about your cell phone ringing but a higher calling which didn't let you sleep at night. 

The people I am going to talk about are not just doing something for their own but they are also helping others lead better lives. It is hard to find a good person that can help you these days but they are still there. You just need to look around and you can find youngsters like these to find it. They are doing what they are passionate about while changing the world around them one small step at a time.

headline: Building 1% Club - AI CFO for your money
about:
Hey, I am Sharan Hegde, better known as Finance With Sharan.

With 1 Crore+ followers across Instagram, YouTube & LinkedIn and X, you have probably seen my finance videos pop up in your feed. But LinkedIn is where I tell a different story. This is where I build in public.

Right now, with a team of 200+ people, I am building something I genuinely believe Indians have been waiting for: an AI-first personal finance app inside 1% Club.

But before I get there, a little backstory.

It started in school, when I could not crack IIT (the classic Indian household story). That setback made me fiercely competitive. In 2019, I chased a promotion as a management consultant. Two years of grind got me a 5% raise and no promotion. Setback two. Then I attempted CAT 2021 dreaming of IIM Bangalore. Setback three.
I am sure this resonates with a lot of you.

So I treated every failure as feedback, and Finance With Sharan was born. The mission was simple: make finance simple, fun, and actually useful.

2 years ago I started the 1% Club to help people become financially independent. Today we are SEBI-licensed (RIA & RA), backed by Gruhas, and profitable. 

My simple problem statement behind all this is that:

Most of us juggle a broker, a bank, three card apps, an insurance portal. Each does one thing okay. None of them helps you think across your full money picture.

That is what we are fixing. An AI co-pilot that sees your complete financial life, answers in plain language, and nudges you before you make a mistake. Not generic internet advice, or an expensive human advisor you do not trust. Something in between, built for the Indian middle that has real money decisions but no one to ask.

Financial independence is a superpower. Less than 1% of people get there in their lifetime.

We are building the thing that gets you there.

about:
Shradha Sharma is the definitive voice of India’s new economy. 
In 2008, when the word “startup” was still making its way into India’s consciousness, she founded YourStory with a simple conviction: every founder’s journey deserved to be heard. 
Born in Bihar, Shradha built what would become the chronicle of India’s entrepreneurial transformation at a time when few believed such stories mattered.
Seventeen years on, the impact of that early conviction is undeniable. 

Shradha has done far more than document the rise of startups. She has actively shaped the ecosystem itself. Her platform has told over 200,000 founder stories, helping unlock more than $10 billion in economic value while helping create over a million jobs across the country. These numbers only begin to capture her impact.

Shradha operates with rare fluidity across India’s most influential circles. She has interviewed Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the late Ratan Tata, engaged with global leaders like Angela Merkel and Steve Wozniak, and brought Union ministers and unicorn founders into conversation with millions of Indians. 
Towards the end of 2015, she contributed by co-authoring the startup India policy. She is a member of the National Startup Advisory Council. 
In 2023, she co-chaired India's G20 S20 agenda on inclusive innovation.

Shradha has never let scale change her priorities. She commands the attention of policymakers and global leaders, yet she brings the same conviction to amplifying first-time founders in Indore, Kochi, or Guwahati. 

She has made entrepreneurship aspirational for an entire generation of Indians who never saw themselves in that role before. Fortune recognised her impact by featuring her in their “40 Under 40 entrepreneurs in India” for three consecutive years. Forbes honoured her with their Power Trailblazers award in 2018.
She started YourStory with personal savings of Rs 1 Lakh and the company is now valued at Rs 350 Crore. 
Today, with over 2.1 million followers on LinkedIn, Shradha’s influence extends well beyond media. Her name has become interchangeable with India’s startup movement itself. You cannot tell the story of India's entrepreneurial transformation over the past two decades without her. 

She made it visible, credible, and unmistakably Indian.

experience.description: trying stuff at the intersection of genAI and content. Part technology, part creativity.

Spent a few months hacking around and building Generative AI apps and games. Autocodepro.com (prompt2code), AlphaCTR.com (YouTube thumbnail generator based on a finetuned stable diffusion model), Godinabox.co (GPT inside WhatsApp), overpoweredcardgame.com and a few more. I built these for fun and to learn everything I can about the space and possible opportunities. The apps cumulatively have over a million users.

My thesis is that generativeAI will transform the skill of writing code into a baseline skill required in all jobs, similar to what English is to many jobs in India. With 100x, I backed Sid and team to go out and teach people to engineer for the AI era the right way — with outcomes and placements in mind and without an overt bias on programming languages — it may one day get abstracted to just English :)

EdTech is notorious for bad actors, but I made the call because this team genuinely cares about the people they’re teaching.

Community software used by some Indian banks, stock broker platforms, insurance companies, and EdTechs. Examples include uNext, Financewithsharan, Ankur Warikoo, and plenty more. Raised a small seed round in 2020.

Our original goal was to build a profitable social media company out of India. While we did get users, monetizing them at scale turned out to be an insurmountable challenge.

Good old services company writing code for businesses across the world. We also had a penchant for running a lot of experiments using the scientific method of hypothesis, experimentation, observation, repetition.

We had a high failure rate across our product experiments with some wins here and there. However, we learned a lot!
